intro: Professionals and everyday users convert pound-feet (lb·ft) to pound-inches (lb·in) when working across imperial and imperial standards in automotive lug nut torque wrench settings, engine dynamometer curves, and industrial fastener specifications. One pound-foot (ft·lbf) equals 12 pound-inches, while 1 pound-inch (in·lbf) equals 0.083333 pound-feet. Whether you are verifying torque specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

faqs.question: How many pound-inches (lb·in) are in 1 pound-foot (ft·lbf) (lb·ft)?
faqs.answer: There are 12 pound-inches (lb·in) in 1 pound-foot (ft·lbf) (lb·ft), which rounds to 12 lb·in for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 pound-inch (in·lbf) equals 0.083333 pound-feet.

faqs.question: How do I convert pound-feet to pound-inches (lb·ft to lb·in)?
faqs.answer: To convert pound-feet to pound-inches, use the formula: lb·in = lb·ft × 12. For example, converting 50 lb·ft gives 600 lb·in.

faqs.question: What is 50 pound-feet in pound-inches?
faqs.answer: 50 pound-feet (lb·ft) equals exactly 600 pound-inches (lb·in) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
